subject: Urban Planning
title: Car-Free Cities: Reclaiming Streets
description: A 60-second lesson on Car-Free Cities: Reclaiming Streets.

hook.text: Ghent, Belgium banned cars from its entire medieval center in 2017. It's now Europe's largest car-free zone.

buildup.text: Oslo removed nearly all parking spaces from its city center, replacing them with bike lanes and benches.

discovery.text: Pontevedra, Spain went car-free and saw CO2 drop 70%, zero traffic deaths, and population growth.

twist.text: Car bans face fierce opposition. Madrid's new car-free zone was reversed by the next mayor, then reinstated.

climax.text: Superblocks in Barcelona close interior streets, creating mini-parks in former parking lots.

punchline.text: Ban the car. Get the city back.

quiz.question: What happened in Pontevedra, Spain after banning cars from the center?
options: Businesses closed and the population declined sharply
CO2 dropped 70%, zero traffic deaths, and population grew
The ban was reversed after six months due to protests
